title: Error funnel breakdown and trace annotator for inference pipelines
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Build an "error funnel" view that breaks down end-to-end inference request failures by pipeline stage (API ingress, auth, routing, model selection, KV cache, batching, model invocation, decoding, transport) and attach persistent, machine-readable failure labels to traces so dashboards and alerting can slice failures by root cause class (timeout, overload, model-error, decode-error, client-protocol, transport).

Scope:
- Instrument tracing hooks in the API gateway and serving runtime to set 'failure_stage' and 'failure_class' span attributes when a request fails or degrades.
- Add derived metrics and logs mapping in the logging pipeline so downstream aggregations (Prometheus/Grafana and Loki) can compute failure funnel rates and stage latencies.
- Create a Grafana dashboard with: funnel waterfall (counts + p95 latency per stage), stage heatmap by model and route, top contributing model variants to model-error class, HTTP/gRPC code breakdown, time series of overall failure-rate by class, and SLO burn view.

Why: Current dashboards lump many failure types together which hides root causes (e.g., overloaded batching vs model OOM vs transient network errors). A stage-aware funnel + trace annotation will speed RCA, reduce alert noise, and power automated fallback logic in routing.

Out of scope for this ticket: automated routing mitigations and runbook automation; those will be follow-ups once signal quality is validated.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing: spans for requests show 'failure_stage' and 'failure_class' attributes for >95% of failures across canary services.
Metrics/logs: logging pipeline produces a 'failure.funnel' derived metric (labels: stage, class, model, route) and a 'failure.latency_by_stage' histogram.
Dashboards: Grafana panel set includes funnel waterfall, stage heatmap, and failure-class time series; dashboards link to representative trace examples.
Alerting: demo alert rule that fires on sudden increase in 'model-error' class for any model variant (test rule on staging).
Docs: short runbook describing how to interpret the funnel, and instrumentation README for engineers.
implementation_notes: Tracing hooks: add a small middleware in gateway (Go) and runtime (C++/Rust shim + Go API) that maps exceptions/errors to canonical 'failure_class' values. Use existing semantic conventions where possible ('otel.status_code', 'http.status_code', 'rpc.status_code').

Failure taxonomy: canonical classes = timeout, overload, model_error, decode_error, auth_error, client_protocol_error, transport_error, quota_exceeded. Each class maps to a short code (e.g., 'model_error').
Log pipeline: update Fluentd filter to inject 'failure_stage' when a span indicates error and to translate gRPC codes to classes for older services that don't emit structured failure_class yet.
Derived metrics: produce Prometheus counter 'redwood_failure_funnel_total{stage, class, model, route}' and histogram 'redwood_failure_stage_latency_seconds{stage}'.
Dashboards: create a Grafana folder 'Observability / Failure Funnel' and implement panels as composable queries so product teams can embed them.
comments: 2026-03-10 Ava Martinez: Initial ticket created after on-call postmortem for INC-2026-03-02. Key asks: distinguish batching overload from model OOMs and correlate with route-level SLOs.

2026-03-11 Rohit Anand: POC of trace annotator pushed to branch feature/trace-annotator; PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4297. Middlewares added for gateway and a lightweight runtime hook. Needs review for performance overhead.

2026-03-12 Design review (Dalia Chen): UX prefers funnel waterfall as primary panel, with drilldown to trace list. Requested clearer color mapping for classes and a compact legend for multi-tenant dashboards.

2026-03-13 Engineering review (Lukas Meyer): agreed to use tag keys 'failure.stage' and 'failure.class' to avoid conflicting with legacy instrumentation. Suggested sampling policy: tag all failed spans, sampled traces for model_error and overload up to 1000/day per service.
2026-03-14 CI: integration tests added for Fluentd mapping; staging dashboards validated against replay of 72h of production logs (replay job: https://ci.redwood.internal/job/replay/3821).
2026-03-14 PM note (Jules Ortega): please include a short training doc for SREs and product owners before release.
monitoring_strategy: Canary: enable annotator on 10% of traffic for gateway and runtime; monitor CPU and p95 latency overhead for 48h.
Signal quality: compare derived failure counts to raw error logs; expect <2% divergence after Fluentd mappings stabilized.
Alerts: temporary alert if annotator increases request p95 by >5% or CPU by >8% on canary nodes.
